Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with a chosen symplectic integrator

Source: R/hmc.R
simp_hmc.Rd

A minimal Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampler that draws each proposal by integrating the Hamiltonian flow of the target with simp_integrate() and accepting it by the Metropolis rule on the total energy. The integrator is a free choice, so this is the smallest complete setting in which the schemes can be compared on a real sampling problem.

Usage

simp_hmc(
  U,
  grad_U,
  init,
  n_iter,
  eps,
  n_steps,
  integrator = "leapfrog",
  mass = NULL,
  warmup = 0L,
  divergence_threshold = 1000
)

Arguments

U

Function mapping a position to the potential energy, U = -log density of the target up to an additive constant.

grad_U

Function mapping a position to the gradient of U.

init

Numeric vector, the starting position.

n_iter

Number of retained iterations.

eps

Positive leapfrog step size.

n_steps

Number of integrator steps per proposal.

integrator

Name of a built-in scheme; see simp_schemes().

mass

Mass matrix M, as in simp_integrate(). Momenta are drawn from N(0, M).

warmup

Number of initial iterations to discard.

divergence_threshold

Energy-error magnitude above which a proposal is counted as divergent and rejected.

Value

A list with the draws matrix (one row per retained iteration, one column per coordinate), the accept_rate, the number of divergent proposals n_divergent, and the integrator used.

Examples

# Sample a correlated 2-D Gaussian.
Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.8, 1), 2)
P <- solve(Sigma)
U <- function(q) 0.5 * as.numeric(t(q) %*% P %*% q)
grad_U <- function(q) as.numeric(P %*% q)
fit <- simp_hmc(U, grad_U, init = c(0, 0), n_iter = 200, eps = 0.2,
                n_steps = 20, warmup = 100)
colMeans(fit$draws)
#> [1]  0.004591804 -0.010837943
